objective: Baseline 10-class semantic segmentation on the official train/val/test split; validates the full pipeline end to end
dataset: DS004 JHU spinal-cord segmentation (porcine, INTRAOPERATIVE post-laminectomy)
train_subjects: unknown - the public release distributes no subject identifier for 56.3% of images (see exp001)
validation_subjects: unknown - the public release distributes no subject identifier for 56.3% of images (see exp001)
test_subjects: unknown - the public release distributes no subject identifier for 56.3% of images (see exp001)
preprocessing: greyscale, resize to 144x352, scale to [0,1]; masks nearest-neighbour
augmentation: horizontal (rostral-caudal) flip p=0.5; gain/brightness jitter p=0.5; Gaussian noise p=0.3
primary_metric: test image-level macro Dice (NaN for classes absent from both prediction and truth)
secondary_metrics: median 0.6967; IQR [0.6316, 0.8061]; SD 0.1159; mean IoU 0.6323; best class Spinal cord 0.9469; worst class Dura/Pia complex 0.2487; best val macro Dice 0.7658 at epoch 21
confidence_interval: 95% bootstrap CI on mean Dice [0.7142, 0.7321] (2000 resamples over images)
notes: PORCINE, INTRAOPERATIVE, POST-LAMINECTOMY. Not lumbar, not transcutaneous, not human. Pipeline validation only. NOT directly comparable to the publication's benchmark figures: the averaging convention differs (we score absent classes as NaN rather than 0) and we did not reproduce their protocol. The bootstrap CI resamples IMAGES, which understates uncertainty relative to resampling animals - animals cannot be resampled because no animal ID exists.

objective: Test whether Monte-Carlo-dropout uncertainty correlates with real segmentation error, whether abstention improves retained performance, and what the worst cases have in common
dataset: DS004 JHU spinal-cord segmentation (porcine, INTRAOPERATIVE post-laminectomy)
train_subjects: unknown - the public release distributes no subject identifier for 56.3% of images (see exp001)
validation_subjects: unknown - the public release distributes no subject identifier for 56.3% of images (see exp001)
test_subjects: unknown - the public release distributes no subject identifier for 56.3% of images (see exp001)
model: U-Net from exp003, bottleneck Dropout2d re-enabled at test time (BatchNorm kept in eval)
runtime: 10 forward passes over the test split
primary_metric: Spearman rho between MC-dropout uncertainty and per-image Dice
secondary_metrics: abstaining on the most-uncertain 30% raises retained Dice from 0.7224 to 0.7644 (+0.0420), with declined images at 0.6245; worst decile Dice 0.5444 vs best decile 0.9095; Spearman Dice vs image contrast +0.5424, vs mean intensity +0.4751
confidence_interval: not computed - rank correlation over all 660 test images
notes: Both uncertainty measures are strongly negatively correlated with Dice, so the signal tracks real error rather than being decorative. Failures concentrate in DARK, LOW-CONTRAST images (worst decile mean intensity 0.25 vs 0.37; contrast SD 0.21 vs 0.28), consistent with poor acoustic coupling or attenuation. PORCINE, INTRAOPERATIVE data: this validates the MECHANISM. It is not a safety claim and the model is not safety-certified.
